text: はっ　はあ　はあ…　これで　おもいのこす　ことは　ない　おぬしに　すべて　たくした　からな　あとは　じいさんの　おむかえを　まつ　ばかりじゃ…
note: おむかえ ('being come for') is a common euphemism for death, from the Buddhist idea that Amida Buddha comes to fetch the dying. He is saying he is only waiting to die; the English softened this to living out his life.
claim: In Japanese, お迎え (omukae) is a euphemism for death, derived from the Buddhist belief that Amida Buddha comes to welcome the dying (raigō).

check.quote: 臨終に、阿弥陀仏が浄土に導くため迎えに来ること。「冥土(めいど)から―が来る」 / 「お迎えが来る」など と言う場合は、しばしば比喩的に「死ぬ」ことを指す。
